collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager keeps courting someone who has said no: tell them firmly, or ask friends to step in.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has told (friend), clearly, that (subject.he/she) is not interested. (friend) keeps bringing flowers anyway, and fish, and songs, and waiting outside (subject)'s hut. (subject) is no longer flattered. (subject.He/she) is uncomfortable. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells (friend), in front of the hut, that the answer is no and will stay no, and that the gifts must stop. (friend) is crushed, and goes away. The gifts stop. (subject) is relieved and sad at once.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject)'s friends have a quiet word with (friend), explaining that no means no. (friend) is embarrassed, apologizes to (subject), and stops. It takes a while before (subject) feels easy around (friend.him/her) again.
